sourceLongSummaries: The session opens with a recap of Holda's commission, Dandelion House, the Feywild party, Lord Endless Ending's bargain, and Menestheus's role in Arithrimos Lamperum. At the Lone Door, the party reviews what they know about the glass key, the cold-iron 27th Room, and the uncertain route home, then describes their readiness and doubts. Menestheus, resigned and still reeling from the time jump, opens the door and steps across the threshold, with Edric and Tarek following.

The party enters a damaged room with smashed furnishings, an occupancy counter, a torn tapestry, humming machinery, and four numbered exits that only open when the whole group passes through together. They choose room 22, a Drankorian chapel with recognizable altars to the Mos Numena and a disturbing carved niche in the rear wall. Edric finds the Night Queen's altar still consecrated, Tarek briefly sticks his hand into the niche and recoils, and the party notes the contrast between the wrecked entry room and the untouched chapel. When they try to go back up toward the entry room, they instead arrive somewhere new.

The party arrives in a machinery-packed room with a two-foot iron window, a desk, and a journal of dated transcriptions. The journal records a speaker learning words, time, eating, drinking, sunset, stars, cold iron, books, roots, leaves, mushrooms, houses, roads, and doors, then feeling abandoned by a teacher and finally describing itself as grown, tall, and becoming houses through trees, roots, leaves, and mushrooms. The party infers that the teacher may be Lord Endless Ending and that the speaker may be the prisoner or house-being; Kaito sits at the desk and briefly hears whispers while writing fragments, and Ayveen confirms with an Arcana check that iron can matter to some fey or other non-material creatures. The beat ends with the party testing the room labels and choosing room 16.

The party enters room 16, a kitchen and dining room, and starts tracking how repeated room numbers fail to connect back in ordinary ways. They move through a mortuary with dissected bodies, an ossuary, and a corpse covered in white mold; sleeping quarters; a revisited mechanical room whose window and exits have shifted; a meeting room; the chapel again; a solarium that steadies Txarro; a bathhouse; and a disappointing labeled room 27 that is only a storeroom. The group concludes that trying rooms at random or visiting as many new numbers as possible may be more useful than mapping every connection. Ayveen proposes sitting still instead of chasing the maze, and the party returns to the chapel, where Menestheus works on the numbers while the party takes a long rest under the growing discomfort of the empty niche.

sourceShortSummaries: After the long rest, Menestheus forms a theory of the room rotations, and the party finds the Dreamer notebook in another mechanical listening room.
The party meets Kalepsis in a fungal greenhouse and learns that the 27th Room is a moving prison-machine threatened by infection and controlled by a glass key.
sourceLongSummaries: At the end of the long rest, Menestheus says the rooms behind the party are moving and that repeated back-and-forth travel should eventually bring the same options around again; he thinks the configuration is static even though the numbers change. The party chooses room 15, another mechanical room with a different window, desk, and notebook titled The Dreamer. Its entries describe mortals as dreaming souls, wanting as something readable, and the speaker seeing the shape of possibility; Menestheus connects this phrase to his book, The Shape of Possibility, and is disturbed when he hears the whisper recognize that he is listening. He records a new entry in the notebook, notices the previous entry dates to the morning he and the order went to the party, and the party reasons that Thalestria may have intentionally changed the house's purpose when she made the bargain.

The party enters room 18, a fungal greenhouse and lab full of terraria, strange helpers, and a body under construction, and meets Kalepsis, an ancient dwarven gardener who claims to have become head of Arithrimos Lamperum after Thalestria's death or disappearance. Kalepsis explains that the house is a prison built around a locked central room whose surrounding wheels move it through space and time so whatever is inside cannot grow out through the wall. She says other rooms became infected, that white fibers colonize flesh before turning victims into aggressive mouth-chested creatures, and that she is using fungal cultures and a golem body so she can leave safely and rebuild the order. She also says the head of the order can open the front door, listeners claimed there is another door inside the 27th Room, the prisoner may be a child kept from growing up or dying, and a glass key can unlock all locked doors including the front door.

Its entries describe mortals as dreaming souls, wanting as something readable, and the speaker seeing the shape of possibility; Menestheus connects this phrase to his book, The Shape of Possibility, and is disturbed when he hears the whisper recognize that he is listening. He records a new entry in the notebook, notices the previous entry dates to the morning he and the order went to the party, and the party reasons that Thalestria may have intentionally changed the house's purpose when she made the bargain.

recapBlocks.title: Kalepsis and the Key
sourceShortSummaries: The party meets Kalepsis in a fungal greenhouse and learns that the 27th Room is a moving prison-machine threatened by infection and controlled by a glass key.
sourceLongSummaries: The party enters room 18, a fungal greenhouse and lab full of terraria, strange helpers, and a body under construction, and meets Kalepsis, an ancient dwarven gardener who claims to have become head of Arithrimos Lamperum after Thalestria's death or disappearance. Kalepsis explains that the house is a prison built around a locked central room whose surrounding wheels move it through space and time so whatever is inside cannot grow out through the wall. She says other rooms became infected, that white fibers colonize flesh before turning victims into aggressive mouth-chested creatures, and that she is using fungal cultures and a golem body so she can leave safely and rebuild the order. She also says the head of the order can open the front door, listeners claimed there is another door inside the 27th Room, the prisoner may be a child kept from growing up or dying, and a glass key can unlock all locked doors including the front door.

recapBlocks.title: Postgame Maze Debrief
sourceShortSummaries: After stopping play, the table discusses the Rubik's-cube room structure, puzzle expectations, and what needs to be recapped next session.
sourceLongSummaries: The group calls the session because several players are tired, then continues out of character to clarify the rotating-room structure. They compare the house to a Rubik's Cube or three-layer cake, discuss how repeated travel between rooms can rotate slices until an entry or exit room comes around, and conclude Menestheus can help handle navigation next time. The table then debriefs the design experience: the numbered-room maze encouraged wayfinding even though it was meant to feel like an unsolvable labyrinth, the room contents sometimes pulled attention away from the spatial puzzle, and clearer cues might have helped. The final recap for sleepers notes that the party met an old dwarf, learned about the mold infection and mouth-chested infected bodies, still has not solved how to leave, and will need a recap next week.
